symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the number of coordinates of source and target vectors.

symbols.name: target length

symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: $F_s$ is the normalized Fourier transform of length-$s$ vectors.
symbols.quote: Write $F_s$ and $P_s$ for the normalized Fourier transform and the coordinate permutation of length-$s$ vectors, and likewise $F_t$ and $P_t$ for length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: $\alpha$ is the parameter that sets the width of the Gaussian weights.

symbols.name: second parameter
symbols.meaning: $\theta$ is a second parameter, chosen so that $\alpha^2\theta>1$.
symbols.quote: The paper uses a second parameter $\theta$, chosen so that $\alpha^2\theta>1$.

symbols.name: Gaussian source map
symbols.meaning: $S$ is the Gaussian-weighted map from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors.
symbols.quote: The identity uses two Gaussian-weighted maps $S,T$ from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: Gaussian target map
symbols.meaning: $T$ is the Gaussian-weighted map from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors.
symbols.quote: The identity uses two Gaussian-weighted maps $S,T$ from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: nearest target coordinate
symbols.meaning: $\ell_j$ is the integer nearest to $tj/s$, for $0\le j<s$.
symbols.quote: Let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest to $tj/s$, with ties rounded upward, for $0\le j<s$, and let $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: rounding error
symbols.quote: Let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest to $tj/s$, with ties rounded upward, for $0\le j<s$, and let $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: $C$ is the map from length-$t$ to length-$s$ vectors that selects the coordinates $\ell_j$.
symbols.quote: Let $C:\mathbb C^t\to\mathbb C^s$ be the map $(Cv)_j=v_{\ell_j}$ that selects these coordinates, let $D:\mathbb C^s\to\mathbb C^s$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, an operator on length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: diagonal map
symbols.meaning: $D$ is the diagonal map on length-$s$ vectors that multiplies entry $j$ by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$.
symbols.quote: Let $C:\mathbb C^t\to\mathbb C^s$ be the map $(Cv)_j=v_{\ell_j}$ that selects these coordinates, let $D:\mathbb C^s\to\mathbb C^s$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, an operator on length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: near-identity operator
symbols.meaning: $N=CTD$ is an operator on length-$s$ vectors.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.
Gaussian resampling replaces the transforms for the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of two integers by transforms on power-of-two axes.
